column1: Architecture is the art and science of designing buildings and structures.
column2: 建筑学是设计建筑物和结构的艺术与科学。

column1: A building reflects the scientific and technological achievements of the age as well as the ideas and aspirations of the designer and client.
column2: 一座建筑不仅体现了那个时代的科学和技术成就，还反映了设计师和业主的理念与愿景。

column1: The appearance of individual buildings, however, is often controversial.
column2: 然而，单个建筑的外观常常引发争议。

column1: The use of an architectural style cannot be said to start or finish on a specific date.
column2: 建筑风格的使用，无法被说成在某个具体日期开始或结束。

column1: Neither is it possible to say exactly what characterises a particular movement.
column2: 同样，也无法准确界定某种特定运动的本质特征。

column1: But the origins of what is now generally known as modern architecture can be traced back to the social and technological changes of the 18th and 19th centuries.
column2: 不过，现在被称为现代建筑的这一概念的起源，可以追溯到18世纪和19世纪的社会与技术变革。

column1: Instead of using timber, stone and traditional building techniques, architects began to explore ways of creating buildings by using the latest technology and materials such as steel, glass and concrete strengthened steel bars, known as reinforced concrete.
column2: 建筑师们不再使用木材、石材以及传统的建筑技术，而是开始尝试利用最新的技术和材料来建造建筑物，这些技术与材料包括钢铁、玻璃，以及由钢筋加固的混凝土。

column1: Technological advances also helped bring about the decline of rural industries and an increase in urban populations as people moved to the towns to work in the new factories.
column2: 技术进步也导致了农村产业的衰落，同时城市人口有所增加，人们纷纷迁往城市，在新工厂中工作。

column1: Such rapid and uncontrolled growth helped to turn parts of cities into slums.
column2: 这种迅速且无法控制的扩张，使城市的某些区域变成了贫民窟。

column1: By the 1920s architects throughout Europe were reacting against the conditions created by industrialisation.
column2: 到20世纪20年代，欧洲的建筑师们开始对工业化带来的状况产生反应。

column1: A new style of architecture emerged to reflect more idealistic notions for the future.
column2: 一种新的建筑风格随之出现，旨在体现更为理想化的未来愿景。

column1: It was made possible by new materials and construction techniques and was known as Modernism.
column2: 这一风格的出现得益于新型材料和建筑技术，因而被称为‘现代主义’。

column1: By the 1930s many buildings emerging from this movement were designed in the International Style.
column2: 到1930年代，许多出自这一运动的建筑都采用了国际风格。

column1: This was largely characterised by the bold use of new materials and simple, geometric forms, often with white walls supported by stilt-like pillars.
column2: 这种风格的特点在于大胆使用新材料，以及简洁的几何形态；常见的设计元素包括白色墙面，这些墙面由类似支柱的结构支撑。

column1: These were stripped of unnecessary decoration that would detract from their primary purpose to be used or lived in.
column2: 这些建筑被去除了所有不必要的装饰，以突出其作为居住空间的本质功能。

column1: Walter Gropius, Charles Jeanneret (better known as Le Corbusier) and Ludwig Mies van der Rohe were among the most influential of the many architects who contributed to the development of Modernism in the first half of the century.
column2: 瓦尔特·格罗皮乌斯、查尔斯·詹尼埃（更广为人知的是勒·柯布西耶）和路德维希·密斯·凡·德·罗是二十世纪上半叶推动现代主义发展的最具影响力的建筑师之一。

column1: But the economic depression of the 1930s and the second world war (1939-45) prevented their ideas from being widely realised until the economic conditions improved and war-torn cities had to be rebuilt.
column2: 然而，20世纪30年代的经济萧条以及第二次世界大战（1939–1945年）使得这些想法未能得到广泛实施。直到经济状况改善之后，那些饱受战争破坏的城市才得以重建。

column1: By the 1950s, the International Style had developed into a universal approach to building, which standardised the appearance of new buildings in cities across the world.
column2: 到了20世纪50年代，国际风格已经发展成为一种通用的建筑方式，它使得全球各地城市中的新建筑在外观上具有标准化特征。

column1: Unfortunately, this Modernist interest in geometric simplicity and function became exploited for profit.
column2: 不幸的是，现代主义对几何简洁与功能的兴趣被滥用于牟利。

column1: The rediscovery of quick-and-easy-to-handle reinforced concrete and an improved ability to prefabricate building sections meant that builders could meet the budgets of commissioning authorities and handle a renewed demand for development quickly and cheaply.
column2: 重新发现这种易于施工的高强度混凝土，以及建筑部件预制能力的提升，使得建筑商能够符合相关主管部门的预算要求，同时还能快速且低成本地完成建筑项目。

column1: But this led to many badly designed buildings, which discredited the original aims of Modernism.
column2: 但这导致了许多设计糟糕的建筑，损害了现代主义最初的宗旨。

column1: Influenced by Le Corbusier’s ideas on town planning, every large British city built multi-storey housing estates in the 1960s.
column2: 受到勒·柯布西耶城市规划理念的影响，20世纪60年代，英国的每个大城市都建起了多层住宅区。

column1: Mass produced, low-cost high-rises seemed to offer a solution to the problem of housing a growing inner-city population.
column2: 大规模生产的低成本高层建筑似乎为解决城市内部人口激增带来的住房问题提供了解决方案。

column1: But far from meeting human needs, the new estates often proved to be windswept deserts lacking essential social facilities and services.
column2: 然而，这些新住宅区远远没有满足人类的需求，往往变成了一片荒凉之地，缺乏必要的社会设施和服务。

column1: Many of these buildings were poorly designed and constructed and have since been demolished.
column2: 许多这些建筑物设计和建造都很糟糕，后来被拆除。

column1: By the 1970s, a new respect for the place of buildings within the existing townscape arose.
column2: 到了20世纪70年代，人们开始重新重视建筑物在现有城市景观中的重要性。

column1: Preserving historic buildings or keeping only their facades (or fronts) grew common.
column2: 保护历史建筑，或者仅保留其外观（立面）已成为一种常见的做法。

column1: Architects also began to make more use of building styles and materials that were traditional to the area.
column2: 建筑师们也开始更多地使用该地区传统的建筑风格和建筑材料。

column1: The architectural style usually referred to as High Tech was also emerging.
column2: 被称为‘高科技’的建筑风格也正在出现。

column1: It celebrated scientific and engineering achievements by openly parading the sophisticated techniques used in construction.
column2: 它通过公开展示建筑中所采用的复杂技术，来庆祝科学与工程的成就。

column1: Such buildings are commonly made of metal and glass; examples are Stansted airport and the Lloyd’s building in London.
column2: 这类建筑通常由金属和玻璃构成；例如斯坦斯特德机场以及伦敦的劳埃德大厦。

column1: Disillusionment at the failure of many of the poor imitations of Modernist architecture led to interest in various styles and ideas from the past and present.
column2: 许多现代主义建筑的拙劣模仿在失败之后引发了人们的失望情绪，这促使人们开始关注过去和现在各种风格与理念的作品。

column1: By the 1980s the coexistence of different styles of architecture in the same building became known as Post-Modern.
column2: 到了20世纪80年代，同一栋建筑中同时存在多种不同风格的建筑风格这一现象被称之为‘后现代主义’。

column1: Other architects looked back to the classical tradition.
column2: 其他建筑师回望古典传统。

column1: The trend in architecture now favours smaller scale building design that reflects a growing public awareness of environmental issues such as energy efficiency.
column2: 当前建筑领域的趋势更倾向于采用规模较小的建筑设计，这反映出公众对于环境问题（如能源效率）的认识日益增强。

column1: Like the Modernists, people today recognise that a well-designed environment improves the quality of life but is not necessarily achieved by adopting one well-defined style of architecture.
column2: 就像现代主义者们一样，当今的人们也认识到，一个设计良好的环境确实能够提升生活质量，但仅仅采用某种特定的建筑风格并不一定能达到这一效果。

column1: Twentieth century architecture will mainly be remembered for its tall buildings.
column2: 二十世纪的建筑主要被铭记于其高楼大厦。

column1: They have been made possible by the development of light steel frames and safe passenger lifts.
column2: 高层建筑的实现得益于轻钢框架和安全电梯的发展。

column1: They originated in the US over a century ago to help meet the demand for more economical use of land.
column2: 它们起源于一个多世纪前的美国，旨在帮助满足对土地更经济利用的需求。

column1: As construction techniques improved, the skyscraper became a reality.
column2: 随着建筑技术的进步，摩天楼成为现实。
